2025-12-31.headline: Shanghai to continue offering free license plates for EVs in 2026
2025-12-31.summary: Shanghai will extend its policy of providing free license plates for electric vehicles (EVs) throughout 2026, renewing a measure originally set to expire at the end of 2025. This policy applies to non-commercial EV purchases and is available to eligible Shanghai residents, companies, and individuals meeting specific social insurance or tax payment criteria. The continuation of this policy underscores Shanghai's commitment to promoting EV adoption, as NEVs already account for over 60% of vehicle registrations in the city, which also hosts major EV players like Tesla and Nio.

2025-11-13.headline: US judges say Starbucks' 'vibe' may justify limits on union apparel
2025-11-13.summary: A U.S. appeals court panel voiced concerns that the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has overreached in regulating employer restrictions on union apparel, specifically in a case involving Starbucks. Judges questioned the NLRB's standard that almost any prohibition on union paraphernalia is unlawful unless "special circumstances" exist, suggesting that companies like Starbucks have a legitimate interest in curating their public image and "vibe." This case follows other circuit court decisions that have reversed NLRB rulings regarding workplace dress codes and union advocacy.

This issue affects multiple such ETFs, demonstrating that their performance lags significantly behind their stated daily objectives.

2025-11-05.headline: BYD Crushes Tesla in the UK: The EV Underdog Just Took the Crown

The trend suggests a maturing EV market where affordability and rapid rollout are becoming more crucial than brand prestige.

2025-11-05.headline: Tesla sales in Germany have cratered from last year, data shows

The decline is attributed to factors including Elon Musk's political rhetoric and increasing competition from European and Chinese EV manufacturers. While Tesla introduced a more affordable Model Y version last month, the impact on demand remains to be seen, with potential future support from a new German EV incentive program starting in January 2026.

The suit claims the car lacked safety features to prevent fires or allow for quick escape, and also names the driver's estate as a defendant due to alleged negligence.
